stem: A nurse is preparing a client for evaluation as a heart-transplant candidate. Which statement best describes the evaluation process?

options.A: It is a multidisciplinary assessment that integrates medical factors with psychosocial, behavioral, adherence, and support-system considerations relevant to transplant candidacy and post-transplant care.
options.B: It consists primarily of one cardiac imaging visit because psychosocial and support factors are assessed only after transplantation.
options.C: It evaluates medical eligibility alone because social support, adherence, substance use, and psychological factors are unrelated to transplant planning.
options.D: It has no structured or guideline-based domains, so each center evaluates candidates without reference to recognized transplant standards.

rationale: The current 2024 ISHLT guideline for cardiac-transplant candidates integrates numerous variables in patient selection and care, and current ISHLT psychosocial recommendations identify psychosocial evaluation as an integral part of transplant candidacy and care planning. Evaluation is therefore multidisciplinary rather than medical-only and includes factors that affect the client's ability to safely undergo and manage transplantation. B and C incorrectly exclude psychosocial/support domains, and D ignores current ISHLT guideline frameworks.
educational_objective: Recognize heart-transplant candidacy evaluation as a multidisciplinary process that includes medical assessment plus psychosocial, behavioral, adherence, and support-system factors relevant to safe long-term transplant care.
source_organization: International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT)
source_document_title: ISHLT Guidelines for the Evaluation and Care of Cardiac Transplant Candidates; ISHLT/APM/AST/ICCAC/STSW Recommendations for the Psychosocial Evaluation of Adult Cardiothoracic Transplant Candidates
source_version_date: Cardiac-candidate guideline published 2024-08-08; psychosocial recommendations published 2018-04-27
source_locator: 2024 ISHLT candidate-guideline overview: integrates numerous variables involved in evaluating patients for transplantation and updates patient-selection criteria and collaborative candidate care. 2018 adult psychosocial recommendations → introductory rationale: transplant/MCS candidates undergo a multifaceted assessment; psychosocial evaluation is integral for patient selection, care planning, interventions, referrals, and post-transplant/post-implant care; recommendations define content/process for comprehensive psychosocial evaluation.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports comprehensive multidisciplinary cardiac-transplant candidate evaluation and inclusion of psychosocial/support factors as integral to selection and care planning.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Referrals/Case Management/Interprofessional Care: coordinate complex evaluations and referrals, collaborate with interdisciplinary teams, assess psychosocial/support needs, and facilitate continuity for clients requiring specialized care.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — multidisciplinary coordination of heart-transplant candidate evaluation
correction_summary: Updated the source to the current 2024 ISHLT cardiac-transplant candidate guideline and retained the ISHLT adult psychosocial consensus for the exact psychosocial-evaluation claim. Replaced vague language about an 'extensive' evaluation with clearly supported multidisciplinary domains and avoided claiming that every transplant center uses one identical testing sequence.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current 2024 ISHLT professional guideline for cardiac-transplant candidates plus ISHLT-led adult psychosocial consensus for evaluation domains.
audit_findings.currentness: The 2024 ISHLT guideline explicitly replaces the 2006 and 2016 cardiac-candidate documents; the 2018 adult psychosocial consensus remains the ISHLT-linked adult evaluation framework at the audit date.

claim_by_claim.stem: Preparing a client for transplant-candidate evaluation is a multidisciplinary Management-of-Care scenario.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because current ISHLT guidance integrates medical candidate variables and identifies psychosocial evaluation as integral to selection and long-term care planning.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because evaluation is not limited to one cardiac test and psychosocial/support assessment occurs during candidacy evaluation.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because support, adherence, behavioral and psychosocial factors are explicitly relevant to transplant selection and care planning.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because ISHLT publishes structured evidence-based guidelines and psychosocial recommendations for candidate evaluation.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Avoids claiming a single universal center-specific test battery or exact number/duration of evaluation appointments.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to the comprehensive nature of transplant evaluation.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B tests medical-test-only thinking, C excludes psychosocial domains, and D denies established standards. Each is plausible but source-inconsistent.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A accurately combines medical and psychosocial/support assessment without overclaiming standardization.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address the scope and structure of transplant evaluation with similar declarative form.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is directly appropriate because the item tests complex referral/evaluation coordination and interprofessional assessment.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited whether the 2018 psychosocial statement is too old after the 2024 candidate guideline. The 2024 guideline is used as the current overarching candidate source, while the ISHLT-linked 2018 statement remains the dedicated adult psychosocial evaluation document. The final claim relies on their complementary roles and does not imply that the older document supersedes the 2024 guideline. No unresolved conflict remains.
